title: Election Commission of India
lead: Parliamentary proceedings to ==remove the CEC== were initiated — unsuccessfully — for the ==first time in Indian history==. The Government replaced the ==CJI with a Union Cabinet Minister== on the collegium earmarked by the SC in [[Anoop Baranwal v. UoI (2023)]], via the ==CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023== — now challenged in [[Jaya Thakur v. UoI]].

items.title: Core Electoral Functions
bullets: ==Superintendence and conduct== of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President & Vice-President
==Preparation and periodic revision of electoral rolls==
==Election scheduling== — poll dates, scrutiny of nominations, announcement of results
==Monitoring election expenditure== of candidates and parties
==Countermanding or cancelling polls== in cases of mass rigging
Conduct of ==by-elections== and delimitation assistance

items.title: Party & Advisory Functions
bullets: ==Registration of political parties== under ==s.29A RoPA==
==Recognition== as national or state parties and ==allotment of symbols==
==Advisory role== to President/Governors on ==disqualification of MPs/MLAs==
Appointment of officers to inquire into electoral disputes; ==requesting staff== from President/Governors
==Enforcing the Model Code of Conduct==
==Electoral reforms== and ==voter awareness campaigns==

items.title: Issues
bullets: ==Lack of transparency in appointments==
==Perceived partisanship== due to executive control over appointments
==Limited control over election machinery== — dependent on state staff
==Weak enforcement of MCC== — not legally binding
==Delayed disqualification== proceedings due to legal loopholes
==Political pressure== — reluctance to act strongly against ruling parties
Weak action against ==hate speech and communal campaigning==
==Under-regulated party funding==, opacity in donations
Slow judicial process in ==election petitions==
==Non-auditable EVMs== — partially addressed by VVPATs

items.title: Solutions
bullets: ==Transparent appointment process== — involve the CJI in the committee
==Codify the MCC== into law with enhanced penalties
==Financial transparency== — full donation disclosure and party audits
==Decriminalisation== — strict disqualification for serious criminal charges
==Technology and innovation== in registration, polling, results
==Public awareness== and voter education
==Judicial oversight== of electoral disputes
==Empower the ECI== with control over election staff and resources

head: Case
Holding
rows: Voters have a ==fundamental right under Art 19(1)(a)== to know candidates' antecedents.
Introduced the ==right to a negative vote==.
A person in ==lawful custody (even unconvicted)== is barred from voting and thus from contesting under RoPA.

items.title: Nature & Provisions
bullets: ECI guidelines regulating parties and candidates — ==no statutory backing==, operating under ==plenary powers under Art 324==
==No new schemes, grants or construction promises== during elections
No use of ==government transport/resources== for campaigning
==No appeals to caste or communal sentiment==
Ministers must not combine ==official visits with electioneering==
Prohibits ==hate speech, bribery, intimidation==

items.title: Issues & Solutions
bullets: ==Non-enforceability== due to lack of legal backing
==Violation by ruling parties== through populist announcements
==Delayed action== reducing MCC to mere advisories; ==weak penalties==
==Hate speech and fake news== not effectively tackled

==Solutions==: grant ==statutory status==; ==graded penalties== (fines, bans); ==real-time tracking and citizen reporting==; collaboration with social media and MeitY; ==greater suo motu powers== for the ECI

items.title: Undertaken
bullets: ==Voting age lowered to 18== (61st CA)
==EVMs and later VVPATs==
==EPICs== (Electoral Photo ID Cards)
==Expenditure limits== and mandatory criminal-background affidavits
==NOTA== since 2013

items.title: Proposed
bullets: ==Simultaneous elections== (Union & State)
==Decriminalisation of politics== — pending legislative action
==State funding of elections==
Regulation of ==inner-party democracy and party funding==
Greater transparency in ==financial declarations==
==Reform of FPTP== — proposed ==two-round voting== in tight contests
==Ban on contesting from multiple seats==

items: ==Pre-2017==: individual donations (₹2,000 anonymous cap), corporate contributions (==7.5% of average net profits==), indirect state subsidies (free airtime); RoPA required ==disclosure above ₹20,000==.
==Finance Act, 2016==: amended ==FCRA== to permit ==foreign-owned Indian companies== to donate.

==Finance Act, 2017==: ==removed corporate donation caps and disclosure requirements==, enabling unlimited anonymous funding; introduced ==Electoral Bonds== via RBI Act, IT Act and Companies Act amendments; exempted parties from disclosing EB donations.

==Electoral Bond Scheme (2018–2024)==: interest-free, tax-exempt instruments sold via SBI up to ==₹1 crore==; purchaser anonymity guaranteed. ==73% of Congress's 2024 donations and 43% of BJP's== came via EBs. ==Struck down (Feb 2024)== for violating ==Art 19(1)(a)== and enabling ==corporate quid pro quo==.

items.title: Corporate, Trust & Individual Donations
bullets: ==Post-2017 surge==: corporate donations were ==88.9% of national parties' funding in 2023–24==; BJP received ==₹2,064.5 crore — 9× more than all others combined==
==Prudent Electoral Trust==: ₹723.6 cr to BJP, ₹156.4 cr to Congress; ==Triumph Electoral Trust==: ₹127.5 cr exclusively to BJP
==Concern==: unlimited corporate funding risks ==crony capitalism==
==Individual==: disclosure mandatory above ₹20,000, but ==72% of BJP's 2023–24 funds came from unknown sources==

items.title: State Funding & Solutions
bullets: ==Indirect support==: free airtime on Doordarshan/AIR, tax exemptions, subsidised utilities
==Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998)==: ==partial state funding== to level the playing field
==Law Commission (1999)==: ==full state funding contingent on internal party democracy==
==Bring political parties under RTI==
==Reintroduce caps on corporate donations== and disclose recipient parties
==Amend s.77 RoPA== to include ==all third-party expenses==
